transcript.text: Shark NZ801UK anti hair wrap upright - suction has gone really weak over the last couple of weeks, barely picks up crumbs. Have emptied the bin. Any ideas before I buy a new one?

Yes, it's worth holding off: suction that faded gradually over a couple of weeks usually points to an airflow problem, which is often a simple, cheap fix rather than a sign the vacuum is finished. Since emptying the bin didn't help, the filters are the next thing to look at before spending on a new one. From what you have described, the most likely cause is a full bin or clogged filters. Weak suction is nearly always airflow. With it switched off (battery out or unplugged), empty the bin or change the bag, then wash the filters in cold water only and leave them to dry fully — at least 24 hours. A damp filter chokes the airflow too. Was the bin full or a filter clogged (and is it sorted), is a filter damaged, or was it all clean already?
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
Bin wasn't full, I empty it every time. I've never washed the filters, didn't know they were there. No burning smell or cut-out, motor sounds normal. Where are they?

On most Shark uprights there's a pre-motor foam and felt filter in the main body, usually visible once the dust bin is lifted off, and a separate post-motor filter behind a cover elsewhere on the body. I can't confirm the exact positions on the NZ801UK, so check the filter diagram in its manual or on Shark's UK support page for that model. Detach the hose and wand and look through each one — a coin dropped through should fall straight out. Check the neck of the floorhead and the bin inlet too. Did you find a blockage and clear it, is there one you can't shift, is the hose split, or was it all clear?
Coin goes through the hose fine, no splits. Wand is clear too, I can see light through it. Still weak suction at the end of the hose though.
Try it on a hard floor with the filters fully dry. Is the suction back to normal now, or still weak?
I haven't washed the filters yet, so it's still weak. Do I wash both the foam and the felt one? Cold or lukewarm water?

Yes, wash both the foam and the felt filter, using cold water only and no detergent; Shark advises cold, so avoid lukewarm or hot. Squeeze and rinse until the water runs clear, then let them air-dry completely for at least 24 hours before refitting, as damp filters can damage the motor. Turn the floorhead over and cut away any hair or thread wrapped round the brush bar (roller), then check it turns freely by hand. Was it tangled (and is it clear now), is the brush bar broken, or was it already clean?
Ok, cold water, no soap. The roller has a bit of fluff but it spins freely. I'll wash the filters and let them dry for 24 hours.

Clogged filters make the motor work harder and run the battery down faster. Wash them in cold water and let them dry fully (24 hours). Were the filters clogged (and are they clean now), or were they clean already?
